answer-er27-484-epsa-comment-period.point: EPSA asks FERC to extend the comment deadline to December 7, 2026, as ISO-NE requested.
answer-er27-484-epsa-comment-period.quote: EPSA respectfully requests that the Commission extend the deadline for submitting comments to December 7, 2026, as requested by ISO-NE.

answer-er27-484-epsa-comment-period.point: EPSA says the extension would line up this comment period with other large load filings expected November 16.
answer-er27-484-epsa-comment-period.quote: The short extension would have the added benefit of aligning the comment period with the other expected large loads filings that will be filed with the Commission on November 16

answer-er27-484-epsa-comment-period.point: EPSA says a 24-day comment period would give parties ample time to review the filing and develop comments.
answer-er27-484-epsa-comment-period.quote: an extension of the comment period in the instant docket to 24 days, or until December 7, 2026, would help to ensure that interested parties have ample time to review and develop comments on the filing

filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.point: ISO-NE sets the Large Load threshold at 50 MW and says that size is reasonable for the New England transmission system.
filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.quote: The definition includes a 50 MW load size which is reasonable for the New England transmission system.

filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.point: A load becomes a Large Load when its gross peak demand rises 50 MW or more above its exempt demand.
filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.quote: when its gross peak demand increases by 50 MW or more relative to its exempt demand

filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.point: Interim Contract Demand Service would last up to seven years, or until the required network upgrades are in service if that takes longer.
filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.quote: Interim Contract Demand Service shall be available for a term of no more than seven years, or the length of time required to place the required Large Load Network Upgrades in-service, whichever is longer

filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.point: Interim and non-firm service would be re-dispatched when the large load's price exceeds $250/MWh.
filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.quote: all or a portion of a Large Load’s Interim Contract Demand Service and Non-Firm Contract Demand Service will be re-dispatched when the Large Load’s applicable LMP exceeds a Large Load Re-Dispatch Price of $250/MWh.

filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.point: Where combined impacts need detailed study, ISO-NE would use reasonable efforts to publish the final system impact study report within 120 days of the preliminary report.
filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.quote: If the Cluster Study and other coordination screening determines that there are combined impacts that need to be studied in detail, then the ISO shall use reasonable efforts consistent with Good Utility Practice to complete the additional coordination analysis (i.e., with the Cluster and other studies) and publish a final Large Load System Impact Study report within 120 days of publishing the preliminary Large Load System Impact Study report.

filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.point: ISO-NE proposes a netting threshold of zero MW, which applies only to Large Loads.
filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.quote: the ISO proposes a netting threshold of zero MW (which applies only to Large Loads).

filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.point: ISO-NE says injection from a generator one or more substations away from the load would likely not fully flow to that load, which is why it limits proximity.
filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.quote: an injection into the transmission system from a Large Load Electrically Proximate Generator that is one or more substations away from a corresponding Electrically Proximate Large Load would likely not fully flow to the Electrically Proximate Large Load

filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.point: The transmission owners say a cost recovery agreement among ISO-NE, the utility and the eligible customer is insufficient to prevent the cost shifting the order raised.
filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.quote: the PTOs believe that a cost recovery agreement among ISO-NE, the relevant transmission owner, and the Eligible Customer taking transmission service on behalf of large loads is an insufficient guarantor of preventing the cost-shifting concerns raised by the Commission in the Show Cause Order.

filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.point: The new tariff text requires a Large Load Eligible Customer to designate enough new capacity resources to cover the Firm Contract Demand Service it requests.
filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.quote: To receive the requested amount of Firm Contract Demand Service for a Large Load, the Large Load Eligible Customer shall designate, or cause to be designated, sufficient new capacity resources to meet the requested amount of Firm Contract Demand Service for the Large Load.

filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.point: Co-located and proximate generators on the expedited path would not count toward regional capacity or take part in the capacity market.
filing-er27-484-isone-large-loads.quote: will not be counted towards the region’s capacity for resource adequacy purposes, will not participate in the capacity market, and will not be accredited using the same method as other ISO-NE generating facilities.
